key_catalyst: Oil surging toward $100 (Brent near $95) as the Middle East conflict deepens, with a record-low yen and spiking yields
reasoning: The dominant intraday catalyst — the Iran/Middle East oil shock — did not stay familiar-and-absorbed today; it ESCALATED in objective magnitude, with crude pushing toward $100 and Brent near $95 versus the $80–90 range that recurred across recent memory, plus a record-low yen and spiking bond yields signaling broad risk-off rather than an idiosyncratic single-name AI wobble. Yet QQQ drifted only -0.39% into the close, a muted response that leaves the fresh supply/FX shock largely unpriced. What remains unresolved is where oil and the yen settle in the Asia/Europe overnight session, precisely the window where this escalating premium tends to re-price.
